segments.text: A team of biologists recently began monitoring a city stream that was restored after decades of concrete channeling. Each

moves through the channel. Workers had planted native grasses and shrubs along both edges to reduce erosion and provide shade. Early data show that their numbers are rising steadily near those areas, while flow measurements suggest the waterway now behaves more like a natural system. Local officials hope these signs will justify similar efforts elsewhere in the region.

gaps.explanationZh: 此處為 “Each ___, the group records...”，表示生物學家每隔固定週期就會記錄一次資料，故需填入表示時間週期的名詞 month，與後文「每月」重複監測的敘述相符。
此空格是動詞 records 的主詞，應與前一句提到的 “A team of biologists” 呼應，指同一批進行監測的人，故填入 group，指稱這個監測團隊。
此處 “the number of young fish” 是特定、已在文中被追蹤觀察的魚群數量，並非泛指任意數量，因此需用定冠詞 the 來限定這個特定的計數對象。
“the number of + 名詞” 是固定搭配，用來表示某類事物的數量，此處指「魚的數量」，故填入介系詞 of 連接 number 與其後的 young fish。
此句主詞為 group，受詞為 the number of young ___，依上下文（新礫石床附近、魚類數量上升）可知監測對象是魚類，故填入 fish 作為被計數的生物。
此處描述年輕魚群出現的空間位置——「靠近新的礫石床」，需要表示鄰近關係的介系詞，故填入 near，說明魚群聚集的地點與礫石床的相對位置。
此處 “new ___ beds” 指的是溪流復育後新形成、供魚類棲息與產卵的礫石堆積地形，依上下文語意應填入 gravel，構成 gravel beds（礫石床）此一具體地貌名詞。
此句主詞 the group 同時搭配兩個並列的動詞 records 與 measures，表示團隊「既記錄又測量」兩件事，因此需要並列連接詞 and 來連接這兩個動詞片語。
measures 之後接的是一個作受詞的名詞子句，說明所測量的內容為「水流動的速度」，故填入疑問詞 how，與 quickly 搭配構成 how quickly（多快）。
此處為子句 “___ moves through the channel” 的主詞，依語意應是在描述水流狀態（呼應後文 flow measurements），故填入 water，作為在渠道中流動的主體。

ctwPassages.sourceParagraph: A team of biologists recently began monitoring a city stream that was restored after decades of concrete channeling. Each month, the group records the number of young fish present near new gravel beds and measures how quickly water moves through the channel. Workers had planted native grasses and shrubs along both edges to reduce erosion and provide shade. Early data show that their numbers are rising steadily near those areas, while flow measurements suggest the waterway now behaves more like a natural system. Local officials hope these signs will justify similar efforts elsewhere in the region.

segments.text: A museum conservation team is studying how sunlight fades the paint on outdoor murals around the city. Researchers

and yellows tend to fade faster than deep blues and greens under the same lamp conditions. The group is also testing several clear coatings that might slow this process without changing how a mural looks. Early results suggest that one coating reduces color loss noticeably, though further trials are still planned before any recommendation is made.

gaps.explanationZh: 此處主詞是 Researchers,後面接受詞 small paint samples 與介系詞 to,構成「expose A to B」(將A暴露於B)的固定搭配,語意上呼應前句「sunlight fades the paint」,說明研究人員讓樣本暴露在紫外線燈下,故填 expose。
此空格為名詞,修飾後面的 samples,構成 paint samples(顏料樣本)。全文主題是研究戶外壁畫顏料(paint)褪色,前句已提到 the paint on outdoor murals,故此處延續同一主題詞 paint,填入 paint 使句意連貫。
動詞 expose 需搭配介系詞 to 才能接受詞,構成「expose...to...」的固定用法,表示「將樣本暴露於強紫外線燈」,故填 to 使句子文法正確。
此處修飾 lamps,表示燈具的種類。全文主旨為研究陽光(含紫外線)如何使顏料褪色,因此燈具應為模擬陽光效果的 ultraviolet(紫外線)燈,與主題「sunlight fades the paint」相呼應,故填 ultraviolet。
此處連接兩個由 Researchers 發出的動作:expose...lamps 與 record how quickly...,屬對等連接詞,用來並列兩個動詞片語,故填 and。
此處引導一個間接問句,作為動詞 record 的受詞,詢問「顏色多快失去亮度」,故填疑問詞 how,與後面的 quickly 組成 how quickly(多快)。
此處為限定詞,修飾 color,表示「每一種顏色」個別的褪色速度都被記錄,呼應下一句提到不同顏色(reds、yellows、blues、greens)褪色速度不同的對比,故填 each。
主詞 each color 為第三人稱單數,動詞需用單數現在式,且句意描述顏色「失去」亮度的持續現象,與 fades 呼應,故填 loses。
此處為動詞 loses 的受詞,指顏色所失去的特性。全句主題是顏料褪色、亮度降低,故填 brightness(亮度),與後文 color loss 語意一致。
此處與 yellows 並列,構成複數顏色名詞 reds and yellows,指「紅色與黃色」這類顏料,呼應下文所述紅、黃色系褪色較深藍、深綠色快,故填 reds。

ctwPassages.sourceParagraph: A museum conservation team is studying how sunlight fades the paint on outdoor murals around the city. Researchers expose small paint samples to strong ultraviolet lamps and record how quickly each color loses its brightness. Bright reds and yellows tend to fade faster than deep blues and greens under the same lamp conditions. The group is also testing several clear coatings that might slow this process without changing how a mural looks. Early results suggest that one coating reduces color loss noticeably, though further trials are still planned before any recommendation is made.

questions.stem: How many swipes does the Standard Plan include per week?

questions.stem: What happens to unused swipes at the end of the week?

options.text: They are refunded in cash to the student

questions.explanationZh: 菜單註明未用完的刷卡次數不會累積到下週,因此答案是次數會過期作廢;文中並未提到現金退款、轉換訪客券或延續使用等做法。

questions.stem: What is the purpose of the guest pricing note?

options.text: To describe how guests can apply for their own meal plan
To inform visitors without a meal plan of the guest cost
To explain that guests can borrow unused student swipes from the weekly plan total
To advertise a discount for returning guests

questions.explanationZh: 訪客定價說明是為了讓沒有餐卡方案的人知道單次用餐需付12美元,並非讓訪客借用學生的刷卡次數,也未提到折扣或申請餐卡方案。

academic.title: Loyalty Programs in Small Retail Business
academic.text:
Small retail businesses often use loyalty programs to encourage customers to return. In a typical program, a shopper earns points for every dollar spent, and those points accumulate toward a reward, such as a discount or a free item. Store owners design point values carefully: too few points per purchase makes the reward feel out of reach, while too many make the program too costly to sustain. Many programs also use reward tiers, giving customers small perks early on and larger rewards after repeated visits. This tiered structure keeps shoppers motivated even before they reach the top level.

Running a loyalty program is not free. Businesses must track points, print or manage digital cards, and absorb the cost of rewards given away. For a small shop with thin profit margins, these costs can add up quickly. Owners therefore have to balance generosity against expense, setting reward thresholds that feel valuable to customers without draining the business's income.

Despite these costs, many small retailers view loyalty programs as worthwhile. Regular customers tend to spend more per visit than occasional shoppers, and a well-designed program can turn a first-time buyer into someone who returns for years, offsetting the price of the rewards themselves.

questions.stem: According to the passage, why do store owners set point values carefully?

options.text: Because setting them too low makes rewards feel unreachable and too high makes costs unsustainable
Because local business associations mandate a standard point-to-dollar conversion rate for all members
Because loyal customers threaten to switch to competitors if the point system feels overly generous
Because digital loyalty platforms automatically cap point values regardless of what owners want

questions.explanationZh: 文章指出點數設定太低會讓獎勵顯得遙不可及,太高則使方案成本難以永續,因此業者須謹慎拿捏點數比例,而非受協會規範、顧客威脅或平台限制。

questions.stem: In the passage, the word "thresholds" is closest in meaning to

options.text: levels a customer must reach before qualifying
promotional messages sent to loyalty program members
physical locations where rewards can be claimed
fixed percentages applied to every single purchase

questions.explanationZh: thresholds 在文中指顧客須達到才能兌換獎勵的門檻,而非兌換地點、宣傳訊息或消費比例。

questions.stem: What can be inferred about occasional shoppers compared to regular customers?

options.text: They tend to receive higher point values than regulars
They tend to spend less per visit than regulars
They tend to never qualify for any loyalty rewards
They tend to complain more often about program costs

questions.explanationZh: 文章暗示偶爾光顧的顧客單次消費通常低於常客,並未提到抱怨、獲得更高點數或完全無法獲得獎勵。

questions.stem: How does the passage relate the idea of program costs to the idea of program benefits?

options.text: It shows that real costs can be offset by spending
It argues that costs always eliminate any real benefit
It treats costs and benefits as unrelated separate concerns
It claims that benefits only appear once programs end

questions.explanationZh: 文章先描述經營忠誠方案的實際成本,接著說明常客消費增加能抵銷這些成本,顯示兩者為有關聯而非互相抵消或無關的概念。

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of the second paragraph?

options.text: To compare loyalty programs across different industries
To explain the practical costs and trade-offs owners face when running a program
To criticize small businesses for adopting loyalty programs
To describe how customers redeem their points

questions.explanationZh: 第二段主要在說明業者經營忠誠方案時面臨的實際成本與取捨,並非批評小型企業、比較產業差異或說明如何兌換點數。

segments.text: Athletes must drink enough water before starting a strenuous workout. Doctors

dehydration during a session. Coaches often schedule brief breaks so players remember to gulp fluids every twenty minutes. In longer competitions, many participants choose special beverages containing dissolved minerals and sugar. They replace what perspiration removes from the body. Restoring those salts swiftly wards off muscle cramps and sustains steady output.

gaps.explanationZh: 主詞為複數的 Doctors，且此句陳述醫生一般性的建議，須用現在式動詞 recommend，後接動名詞 sipping，符合「recommend + V-ing」的固定用法。
此處修飾 amounts（少量），與後文「sipping」小口啜飲的動作相呼應，故用形容詞 small 表示少量飲水，而非大量。
roughly 修飾後面的時間 an hour，表示「大約、粗略地」，說明建議喝水的時間點並非精確一小時，而是概略估計。
與前面的 an 及 roughly 搭配，構成 roughly an hour beforehand（運動前大約一小時），為文中建議提前喝水的具體時間單位。
為新句開頭，須大寫；Persistent（持續的）修飾 fatigue，說明脫水徵兆中的疲勞是持續性而非偶發的，語意上與 dizziness、dry mouth 並列為警訊症狀。
與 fatigue、dry mouth 並列，屬於輕度脫水的常見症狀之一，意指「頭暈」，符合句意列舉脫水徵兆的邏輯。
後接以母音開頭的 unusually，依英文文法須使用不定冠詞 an 而非 a，用來修飾 mouth。
dry mouth（口乾）與 fatigue、dizziness 同為脫水的徵兆之一，符合上下文列舉症狀的語境。
can 為情態動詞，表示這些症狀「可能」顯示輕度脫水，語氣上屬於可能性推測，而非肯定陳述，符合句意的不確定性。
mild 修飾 dehydration，表示這些症狀反映的是輕微、初期的脫水狀況，而非嚴重脫水，與句中列舉的輕微不適徵兆相符。

ctwPassages.sourceParagraph: Athletes must drink enough water before starting a strenuous workout. Doctors recommend sipping small amounts roughly an hour beforehand. Persistent fatigue, dizziness, or an unusually dry mouth can signal mild dehydration during a session. Coaches often schedule brief breaks so players remember to gulp fluids every twenty minutes. In longer competitions, many participants choose special beverages containing dissolved minerals and sugar. They replace what perspiration removes from the body. Restoring those salts swiftly wards off muscle cramps and sustains steady output.

academic.title: How Sound-Absorbing Materials Reduce Urban Noise
academic.text:
Cities can be noisy places, especially near busy roads. Engineers have found that certain materials can help lower this noise. These materials are called sound-absorbing materials, and they are usually full of tiny holes or open spaces. When sound waves hit a porous material, some of the sound energy gets trapped inside the small holes instead of bouncing back into the air. This means less noise reaches nearby homes, schools, and parks.

Common sound-absorbing materials include foam panels, certain types of concrete, and layered fabric screens. Engineers often place these materials in walls or barriers built along highways. Tests show that a well-placed barrier can lower noise levels by a noticeable amount, making conversations and daily activities easier for people who live close by.

Placement matters as much as the material itself. A barrier works best when it stands close to the noise source and blocks a direct path to the area it protects. Height and length also affect how much sound gets through. Because of this, city planners often work with acoustic engineers to decide exactly where a noise barrier should go before it is built.

questions.stem: According to the passage, what happens when sound waves hit a porous material?

options.text: Some sound energy becomes trapped inside the small holes
The material converts sound into heat that heats nearby buildings
The waves are reflected back at a higher volume
The waves pass straight through without change

questions.explanationZh: 文章說明聲波撞擊多孔材料時,部分聲能會被困在細小孔洞中,而不是直接穿透、以更大音量反射,或被轉換成熱能加熱建築物。

questions.stem: In the passage, "porous" most nearly means

options.text: resistant to weather damage
extremely heavy
full of tiny openings
brightly colored

questions.explanationZh: porous 在文中指材料內部布滿細小孔洞,並非指沉重、色彩鮮豔或防風化。

questions.stem: What can be inferred about a barrier that is not placed close to a noise source?

options.text: It requires no acoustic engineering at all
It will completely eliminate all nearby noise
It must be made of a different material
It will likely block sound less effectively

questions.explanationZh: 文章暗示隔音牆若不靠近噪音來源,效果會較差,並未說明能完全消除噪音、需換材質或不需要聲學工程師參與。

questions.stem: How does the second paragraph build on the idea introduced in the first paragraph?

options.text: It restates the first paragraph without adding anything new
It switches to an unrelated topic entirely
It builds on that explanation with concrete material examples
It disputes the first paragraph's claim about how sound absorption actually works in practice

questions.explanationZh: 第二段承接第一段對吸音原理的說明,進一步舉出實際材料(泡棉、混凝土、隔音屏)與其應用方式,並非反駁前段論點,也未轉向無關主題或單純重複。

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of the third paragraph?

options.text: To criticize city planners for poor decisions
To explain that where a barrier is placed also affects how well it reduces noise
To describe the history of noise barrier design
To argue that material choice does not matter

questions.explanationZh: 第三段主要說明隔音牆的擺放位置也會影響降噪效果,並非表示材質不重要、批評城市規劃者或介紹隔音牆歷史。

segments.text: Supermarket planners carefully design the layout of aisles so that shoppers move through the store in a predictable pattern. Because

the perimeter. Special displays near the end of each row showcase featured merchandise that retailers want patrons to notice. Small, inexpensive products positioned near checkout lines encourage impulse purchases from consumers with little else to occupy attention. Researchers who study shopping patterns argue that this arrangement, though seemingly convenient, maximizes the time and money a typical visitor spends inside the shop.

gaps.explanationZh: 此句的邏輯主詞需與後文「walk along the outer edges」的動作者一致，且呼應前句提到的 shoppers（顧客），故填入 customers，指稱在賣場中走動的消費者。
tend 之後須接不定詞 to walk，構成「tend to + 原形動詞」的固定搭配，表示「傾向於做某事」，故填 to。
此處描述顧客「沿著」外側走動的路徑，need 一個表示沿著方向移動的介系詞，故填 along，與 walk 搭配構成 walk along。
edges 前需要形容詞修飾，指的是賣場「外側」的邊緣（與後段 perimeter 呼應，皆指外圍區域），故填 outer。
此字修飾整個子句，表示顧客「首先」會走外圍動線，之後才會進入其他區域，與全文描述的動線先後順序相符，故填 first。
popular 後需要一個可與 such as dairy and produce 對應的複數名詞，指「乳製品和農產品」這類受歡迎的「商品」，故填 goods。
此處為列舉例子的固定用法 such as，意為「例如」，用來引出 dairy and produce 這兩個具體例子，故填 as。
dairy 與 produce 是兩個並列的名詞，中間需要對等連接詞連接兩者，故填 and。
主詞 goods 為複數，且此句為被動語態描述商品「被放置」在外圍，故須用複數 be 動詞 are 搭配 placed，填入 are。
此處指商品被放置的位置是「沿著」賣場外圍（perimeter），與句意「沿著周邊擺放」相符，故填 along，與前面 along the outer edges 呼應同一種空間描述方式。

ctwPassages.sourceParagraph: Supermarket planners carefully design the layout of aisles so that shoppers move through the store in a predictable pattern. Because customers tend to walk along the outer edges first, popular goods such as dairy and produce are placed along the perimeter. Special displays near the end of each row showcase featured merchandise that retailers want patrons to notice. Small, inexpensive products positioned near checkout lines encourage impulse purchases from consumers with little else to occupy attention. Researchers who study shopping patterns argue that this arrangement, though seemingly convenient, maximizes the time and money a typical visitor spends inside the shop.

academic.title: Standardizing Measurement Units in the Industrial Era
academic.text:
Before the widespread standardization of measurement units, factories across a single region often relied on inconsistent local systems inherited from earlier eras. A bolt manufactured to one town's definition of an inch might differ noticeably from a supposedly identical bolt produced in a neighboring town, since each locality had historically calibrated its own tools and reference standards independently. As industrial production expanded and components increasingly needed to interlock precisely across factories, these discrepancies produced costly manufacturing errors: parts that should have fit together failed to align, machinery malfunctioned, and entire production runs sometimes had to be discarded.

Recognizing the mounting economic toll of this fragmentation, industrialists and government officials began lobbying for a uniform national standard. Committees were formed to compare competing regional definitions and select a single reference, one that manufacturers throughout the country would be legally required to adopt. Legislatures eventually codified these standards into law, mandating their use in commerce and manufacturing alike.

The transition proved gradual rather than immediate. Established manufacturers resisted retooling their equipment, citing the expense, and it took years of enforcement before the new standard achieved near-universal compliance. Nevertheless, once adopted, standardized measurement dramatically reduced the errors that had long plagued cross-regional manufacturing, enabling the kind of interchangeable-parts production that later defined modern industry.

questions.stem: According to the passage, what problem did inconsistent local measurement units create as industrial production expanded?

options.text: Local factory workers received unequal wages across the region
Parts made to different local standards often failed to fit
National legislatures completely banned trade between neighboring regions
Manufacturers were forced to consolidate all factories into one city

questions.explanationZh: 文章指出隨著工業生產擴張,各地不一致的度量單位導致零件無法精準吻合,造成成本高昂的製造錯誤,並非工資不均、工廠被迫遷移或禁止跨區貿易。

questions.stem: In the passage, the word "codified" is closest in meaning to

options.text: delayed for further review
formally written into law
kept secret from the public
put into practice

questions.explanationZh: codified 在文中指將標準正式訂入法律,並非發明、秘密隱藏或暫時中止。

questions.stem: What can be inferred about manufacturers who resisted the new standard?

options.text: They saw the upfront cost as not worth it for now
They manufactured products that never required any precise measurement standards at all
They had voluntarily switched to the new standard even before it was required by law
They were permanently exempt from the law by special government provision

questions.explanationZh: 文章暗示抗拒採用新標準的製造商,是因為認為當下改裝設備的花費過高並不划算,而非法律上永久豁免或早已採用該標準。

questions.stem: How does the final paragraph relate to the paragraph before it?

options.text: It shows that the standard described earlier was ultimately abandoned
It disputes the claim that a national standard was ever created
It describes the difficult, gradual process of adopting the standard that the previous paragraph explains was legally mandated
It introduces an entirely unrelated historical event

questions.explanationZh: 最後一段承接前段所述的法定標準,進一步描述採用過程其實緩慢而艱難,並非表示標準遭到廢除或提出無關的歷史事件。

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of the passage as a whole?

options.text: To criticize government officials for delaying standardization
To trace how inconsistent measurement units were reformed into a national standard during industrialization
To compare measurement systems used in different countries today
To argue that industrialization would have succeeded without standardized measurement

questions.explanationZh: 全文主旨在追溯工業化時期度量單位如何從各地不一,逐步改革為全國統一標準,並非主張標準化毫無必要或批評政府延遲改革。
